docs.title: Implementation Notes
docs.text:
• Treat docked and modal variants as separate layout systems. Docked uses 48dp dates and dropdown-menu affordances; modal uses 40dp dates, 72dp x 36dp year chips, and explicit range-selection geometry.
  • The type-style rows in the viewer are composite previews rather than directly useful scalar values. Use the accompanying font, size, line-height, weight, and tracking tokens for implementation.
  • Modal range selection adds distinct container and in-range tokens, including md.comp.date-picker.modal.range-selection.container.shape, md.comp.date-picker.modal.range-selection.active-indicator.container.color, and in-range state-layer colors.
  • Modal and modal-input surfaces both resolve their main container elevation through md.sys.elevation.level3; the modal range-selection container resolves through md.sys.elevation.level0.
  • The MD3 page currently exposes duplicated misspelled opcaity token/label variants for modal range-selection hover, focus, and pressed state-layer opacity. Preserve the canonical token names from the page if you need to mirror the source exactly.

docs.title: Summary
docs.text:
• Material Design 3 dialogs expose two active token sets in the live token viewer: Dialog - Basic and Dialog - Full screen.
  • Basic dialogs use a 28dp extra-large container radius with level 3 elevation, while full-screen dialogs use a 0dp container radius and keep the main container at level 0.
  • Shared action affordances in both variants use label-large typography and primary-colored labels and state layers.
  • Basic dialog title text maps to headline-small and supporting text maps to body-medium; full-screen dialog headlines map to title-large.
  • Hover, focus, and pressed state-layer opacity tokens are surfaced through md.sys.state.*.state-layer-opacity system tokens.

docs.title: Implementation Notes
docs.text:
• Treat basic dialogs as surfaced cards with a surface-container-high fill, 28dp corners, 24dp outer padding, and min/max width constraints of 280dp to 560dp.
  • Reuse label-large typography for dialog actions in both variants, and map hover, focus, and pressed state opacities to the surfaced md.sys.state.*.state-layer-opacity tokens.
  • Full-screen dialogs keep the container, header, and action bar flat at rest, then elevate the header and action bar to level 2 while scrolling.
  • Basic dialog titles and subheads align to headline-small; full-screen headers align to title-large; supporting text aligns to body-medium.

docs.title: Divider MD3 Specs
docs.text: Source: https://m3.material.io/components/divider/specs Collected: 2026-05-25

docs.title: Summary
docs.text:
• Divider exposes one active token set in the live viewer: Divider with Default, Light context chips.
  • The component token surface is intentionally small: a 1dp thickness token and a single color token resolved from md.sys.color.outline-variant.
  • The measurements spec distinguishes full-width, inset, and middle-inset placements rather than variant-specific token sets.
  • Insets are 16dp from the left edge for both inset styles; middle-inset additionally applies a 16dp right inset.
  • Supporting-text dividers use a 4dp gap above the text and 8dp right and bottom margins in the illustrated layout.

docs.title: Implementation Notes
docs.text:
• Model divider rendering as a 1dp rule whose default enabled color comes from md.sys.color.outline-variant.
  • Keep layout variants separate from token resolution: full-width, inset, and middle-inset are spacing patterns, not distinct token sets.
  • Use 16dp leading inset for list-style dividers and add a matching 16dp trailing inset only for middle-inset placements.
  • When pairing a divider with supporting text, preserve the 4dp gap above the text and the 8dp right and bottom margins from the measurement spec.

docs.title: Extended FABs MD3 Specs
docs.text: Source: https://m3.material.io/components/extended-fab/specs Collected: 2026-05-25

docs.title: Summary
docs.text:
• The active Extended FAB token viewer exposes nine expressive token sets: three size sets and six color mappings.
  • Resolved values below use the viewer's default Android / 1P Baseline / Light / Default-contrast context. The viewer also exposes Dark, Medium contrast, and High contrast variants.
  • The expressive size scale is 56dp small, 80dp medium, and 96dp large, with icon sizes of 24dp, 28dp, and 36dp and rounded corner sizes of 16dp, 20dp, and 28dp.
  • Small, medium, and large label text map to md.sys.typescale.title-medium, md.sys.typescale.title-large, and md.sys.typescale.headline-small respectively.
  • All six active color mappings share the same state behavior: enabled, focused, and pressed stay at 6dp elevation; hovered rises to 8dp; hover opacity is 0.08; focus and press opacity are 0.1.
  • The page's Measurements section explicitly states a 16dp outer margin. Other concrete size and padding values are sourced from the live size token sets because the measurement diagrams are image-first.

docs.title: Implementation Notes
docs.text:
• Treat the baseline extended FAB as deprecated. New work should target the expressive small, medium, and large size sets instead of the legacy baseline configuration.
  • Support six active color mappings: primary-container, secondary-container, tertiary-container, primary, secondary, and tertiary. The spec explicitly allows all six as equivalent contrast-safe styles.
  • Keep state-layer color aligned with the foreground icon and label-text color for the non-default mappings; the spec calls this out in the States guidance.
  • Hover is the only interaction state that changes elevation, rising from 6dp to 8dp. Focused and pressed preserve the base 6dp elevation and vary only the state-layer treatment.
  • Small/medium/large typography scales are materially different, so size changes should switch typography tokens rather than only scaling container dimensions.
  • The live token viewers for the solid primary, secondary, and tertiary mappings still contain deprecated compatibility rows; those values should not be wired into new expressive implementations.

docs.title: FAB Menu MD3 Specs
docs.text: Source: https://m3.material.io/components/fab-menu/specs Collected: 2026-05-25

docs.title: Summary
docs.text:
• The active FAB menu token viewer exposes seven non-deprecated token sets: one shared geometry set, three close-button color sets, and three list-item color sets.
  • Resolved values below use the viewer's default Android / 1P Baseline / Light / Default-contrast context, with Standard motion, Static font, and no iOS dark elevation override.
  • The common set fixes both the close button and menu item height at 56dp, uses fully rounded corners, and sets the menu-item padding rhythm to 24dp leading, 8dp icon-label spacing, 24dp trailing, and 4dp between-item spacing.
  • Close-button color sets use solid primary, secondary, and tertiary fills with on-* foreground colors; list-item color sets use the corresponding *-container fills with on-*-container foreground colors.
  • Hover is the only interaction state that raises elevation to 8dp. Focused and pressed keep 6dp elevation, while state-layer opacities follow the standard MD3 0.08 hover and 0.1 focus/press values.
  • The Measurements section explicitly calls out a 56dp close button, 16dp outer FAB margins, a 40dp opened bottom margin from medium FABs, a 56dp opened bottom margin from large FABs, and a recommended 4dp web gap between the FAB and menu.

docs.text: State-layer opacity rows below use the live token viewer's displayed values. The embedded payload preserves the semantic source tokens but omits the resolved numeric opacity in resolvedValue.

docs.title: Measurements
docs.text:
Category Item Value Notes Geometry Close button size 56dp Explicitly called out in Measurements and reinforced by the common token set. Geometry Close button icon size 20dp From the common token set. Geometry Close button corner treatment Fully rounded From md.comp.fab-menu.close-button.container.shape. Geometry Close button between space 8dp From the common token set. Geometry Menu item height 56dp Menu items share the same measurements as the medium button specs. Typography Menu item label text Google Sans Text / 500 / 16pt / 24pt Mapped to md.sys.typescale.title-medium. Geometry Menu item icon size 24dp From the common token set. Geometry Menu item corner treatment Fully rounded From md.comp.fab-menu.menu-item.container.shape. Geometry Menu item base elevation 0dp md.sys.elevation.level0, normalized from a unit-only payload entry. Geometry Menu item leading space 24dp From the common token set. Geometry Menu item icon-label space 8dp From the common token set. Geometry Menu item trailing space 24dp From the common token set. Geometry Menu item between space 4dp From the common token set. Placement FAB outer margin 16dp The spec explicitly says the FAB should always have 16dp margins. Placement Medium FAB opened bottom margin 40dp The opened menu places the close button higher to align with the top of the medium FAB. Placement Large FAB opened bottom margin 56dp The opened menu places the close button higher to align with the top of the large FAB. Placement Anchor point Top trailing corner The close button and FAB share the same top trailing anchor position. Motion Expansion direction From the FAB's top trailing edge Explicitly called out in Measurements for smooth animation. Web Recommended FAB-to-menu gap 4dp The gap can vary on web, but 4dp is recommended. Web Baseline behavior source Baseline menu component The web FAB menu inherits states and specs from the baseline menu component.
  • The FAB menu animates from the top trailing edge of the FAB to ensure a smooth animation.
  • Larger FABs will place the FAB menu slightly higher, with larger margins underneath.

docs.title: Implementation Notes
docs.text:
• Keep the geometry token set separate from the color token sets in implementation. The spec treats the close button and list-item layout as common across all color variants.
  • Use solid theme colors for the close button and container theme colors for list items. The page's color section and token viewer align on that distinction.
  • Wire hover to md.sys.elevation.level4 and focus/press to md.sys.elevation.level3 for both close buttons and list items.
  • Treat menu-item base elevation as md.sys.elevation.level0 even though the raw payload serializes the value without an explicit numeric component.
  • Preserve the 24dp / 8dp / 24dp menu-item internal spacing and the 4dp between-item gap; those values materially shape the menu's visual rhythm.
  • On web, keep the FAB menu visually tied to the invoking FAB and start from the baseline menu behavior, with a recommended 4dp separation.

docs.title: Summary
docs.text:
• Material Design 3 FAB specifications covering three current tonal color variants and three current size variants (baseline 56 dp, medium 80 dp, large 96 dp).
  • Four interactive states documented for color variants: Enabled, Hovered, Focused, and Pressed.
  • Color values were scraped from the live FAB token viewer resources for the Default / Light expressive context.
  • Baseline (default) size measurements come from the Specs page Measurements section; live token viewer omits a dedicated FAB - Size - Default table, so values are sourced from the FAB measurements diagram.
  • Deprecated baseline token sets, including Small FAB and legacy surface variants, are excluded from this document.

docs.title: Icon Buttons MD3 Specs
docs.text: Source: https://m3.material.io/components/icon-buttons/specs Collected: 2026-04-25

docs.title: Summary
docs.text:
• Material Design 3 icon button specifications covering four color variants (Filled, Tonal, Outlined, Standard) and five size variants (Xsmall, Small, Medium, Large, Xlarge).
  • Five interactive states documented for color variants: Enabled, Disabled, Hovered, Focused, and Pressed.
  • Toggle icon button selected and unselected states are included where present in the MD3 token set.
  • Values and source tokens were scraped from the live token viewer payload for the Default / Light context.

docs.title: Summary
docs.text:
• The live Lists token viewer exposes two UI-selectable token sets: List - Common and List - Expand, both shown in the Default, Light context.
  • List - Common carries the main implementation surface: enabled, selected, disabled, hover, focus, pressed, and dragged state colors plus shared spacing, shape, and typography tokens.
  • Core container heights are 56dp for one-line items, 72dp for two-line items, and 88dp for three-line items; expressive icon slots shrink to 20dp while baseline icon slots remain 24dp.
  • The baseline layout table adds concrete alignment constraints: 16dp leading padding, 24dp trailing padding, 48dp minimum targets, and 16dp/24dp divider insets.
  • The embedded payload also contains hidden List - Reveal and List - Reorder token-set records, but they are not selectable in the visible spec viewer, so this document follows the UI-visible sets only.

docs.title: Implementation Notes
docs.text:
• Prefer the expressive list variant for new work; baseline remains available but the page explicitly recommends expressive lists for current designs.
  • Keep selected-state colors wired to secondary-container and on-secondary-container, while hover, focus, pressed, and dragged overlays come from the corresponding md.sys.state.* opacity tokens.
  • Treat list layout and list styling separately: the standard and segmented styles do not change behavior, but segmented lists add a 2dp gap and rounded expressive shapes.
  • Preserve the baseline alignment contract for mixed-content rows: 16dp leading padding, 24dp trailing padding, and at least 48x48dp interactive targets.
  • Model the expand interaction as a separate style surface: it uses its own trailing-icon container colors and a fully rounded trailing-icon shape on top of the large rounded expand container.
  • Ignore the payload-only List - Reveal and List - Reorder token sets unless the MD3 spec starts exposing them in the visible selector or the user asks for those hidden sets explicitly.

docs.text: Source: https://m3.material.io/components/loading-indicator/specs Collected: 2026-04-30

docs.title: Summary
docs.text:
• The live MD3 token viewer exposes a single active token set, Loading indicator, with one shape row, three size rows, and four color rows.
  • The token viewer's context selector offers Theme values Light and Dark plus Contrast values Default, Medium contrast, and High contrast; the resolved values below were collected from the default light context.
  • Default loading-indicator colors map the active indicator to md.sys.color.primary and the container to md.sys.color.secondary-container; contained colors map to md.sys.color.on-primary-container and md.sys.color.primary-container.
  • The Measurements section and token viewer agree on a 48dp overall size and a 38dp shape container width, with the shape rendered as fully rounded.

docs.title: Implementation Notes
docs.text:
• Prefer the expressive vertical-menu token sets for new work and keep the baseline set only for compatibility paths.
  • Treat standard and vibrant mappings as separate style families; their token namespaces and color roles differ materially.
  • Preserve support for hover, focus, pressed, disabled, and focus-indicator states because each token set exposes state-specific overrides.
  • Where the token viewer exposes shape or elevation only as previews, keep those values marked visual-only unless another MD3 source provides concrete numeric values.

docs.title: Navigation Bar MD3 Specs
docs.text: Source: https://m3.material.io/components/navigation-bar/specs Collected: 2026-05-26

docs.title: Summary
docs.text:
• The current flexible navigation bar spec exposes three active token sets: Nav bar - Common, Nav bar - Item - Vertical, and Nav bar - Item - Horizontal.
  • The shared flexible bar uses a surface-container container color, 3dp container elevation, a square container shape, 24dp icons, and a fully rounded active indicator.
  • Compact-window navigation uses vertical items with a 56x32dp active indicator, 6dp top and bottom padding, and a 4dp icon-label gap; medium-window navigation switches to horizontal items with a 40dp active indicator and fixed-width item slots.
  • The baseline navigation bar remains documented as a legacy section: it is 80dp tall, keeps a 64x32dp active indicator, and adds focus-indicator plus deprecated badge rows that do not appear in the current flexible viewer.

docs.title: Implementation Notes
docs.text:
• Prefer the flexible navigation bar for new work. The spec explicitly marks the baseline navigation bar as no longer recommended.
  • Compact-window implementations should use the vertical item metrics, while medium-window implementations should switch to the horizontal item metrics and fixed-width item slots.
  • The flexible bar container is square (md.sys.shape.corner.none) while both the current and baseline active indicators remain fully rounded (md.sys.shape.corner.full).
  • The flexible viewer does not expose badge tokens; when badges are implemented on the current navigation bar, use the dedicated badge spec for badge-specific color behavior.
  • The vertical and horizontal label-text rows expose only a preview in the viewer, so the implementation-relevant typography should be taken from the shared md.sys.typescale.label-medium source token.

docs.title: Navigation Rail MD3 Specs
docs.text: Source: https://m3.material.io/components/navigation-rail/specs Collected: 2026-07-08

docs.title: Summary
docs.text:
• Two modern variants: Collapsed (96 dp wide, vertical items) and Expanded (220–360 dp, horizontal items)
  • Items use a fully-rounded active indicator (md.sys.shape.corner.full)
  • Container is flat (md.sys.elevation.level0); expanded modal overlay uses md.sys.elevation.level2 (3 dp)
  • Collapsed container: 96 dp wide (narrow: 80 dp); top space 44 dp; items spaced 4 dp vertically
  • Expanded container: 220–360 dp wide; top space 44 dp; items 0 dp apart; 20 dp trailing vertical space
  • Item container height: 64 dp standard, 56 dp short; icon size 24 dp
  • Vertical active indicator: 32 dp × 56 dp; horizontal active indicator: 56 dp tall, 16 dp leading/trailing
  • Label text: Label Medium (vertical layout) and Label Large (horizontal layout)
  • Baseline navigation rail is deprecated — replace with the collapsed navigation rail
  • The baseline token set prefix is md.comp.navigation-rail; new token set prefixes are md.comp.nav-rail.*

docs.title: Implementation Notes
docs.text:
• The new collapsed rail (md.comp.nav-rail.collapsed) replaces the baseline rail (md.comp.navigation-rail). Width is 96 dp (standard) or 80 dp (narrow), vs. 80 dp fixed for baseline.
  • Use vertical layout (md.comp.nav-rail.item.vertical.*) in the collapsed rail; use horizontal layout (md.comp.nav-rail.item.horizontal.*) in the expanded rail.
  • Active indicator is always fully rounded (md.sys.shape.corner.full). The indicator stretches to a 32×56 dp pill in vertical layout and fills the full row (56 dp tall) in horizontal layout.
  • The expanded modal variant uses md.sys.elevation.level2 (3 dp) and large rounded corners on the right edge (md.sys.shape.corner.large), while the docked expanded variant is flat with no rounding.
  • Both active and inactive items share the same state-layer opacity values: hover=0.08, focus=0.1, press=0.1.
  • Inactive state-layer color is the same token as active (md.sys.color.on-secondary-container) except for inactive icon/label colors which use md.sys.color.on-surface-variant.
  • Typography: vertical items use md.sys.typescale.label-medium (12 pt), horizontal items use md.sys.typescale.label-large (14 pt).
  • Token values above are resolved for Default, Light context.

docs.text: Source: https://m3.material.io/components/progress-indicators/specs Collected: 2026-03-12

docs.title: Summary
docs.text:
• The primary token viewer exposes three non-deprecated token sets: shared common tokens plus linear and circular variant-specific baseline tokens.
  • Shared common tokens provide current color values and shape previews; the shape rows render as circular previews but do not expose textual numeric values.
  • Linear baseline geometry centers on a 4dp track, 10dp wavy height, 3dp wave amplitude, and 40dp wave wavelength, with a 20dp wavelength for indeterminate waves.
  • Circular baseline geometry centers on a 40dp size, 48dp wavy size, 4dp track thickness, 1.6dp wave amplitude, and 15dp wave wavelength.
  • The Measurements section explicitly states a 4dp screen-edge inset for linear indicators and defines amplitude and wavelength, but its remaining figure callouts are image-only in accessible text.

docs.title: Implementation Notes
docs.text:
• Model shared colors separately from variant-specific geometry. Linear and circular sizing is not encoded in the common token set.
  • Treat the shared shape tokens as fully rounded/circular until another source exposes a resolved radius token; the rendered token previews use a circular-shape class and no numeric text.
  • Support both flat and wavy linear indicators; expressive linear geometry depends on wave height, amplitude, and wavelength tokens rather than only track thickness.
  • Keep deprecated thick token groups out of default implementation paths unless you intentionally need archived compatibility behavior.

docs.title: Radio button MD3 Specs
docs.text: Source: https://m3.material.io/components/radio-button/specs Collected: 2026-05-26

docs.title: Summary
docs.text:
• Radio button exposes one active token set in the live viewer: Radio Button with Default, Light context chips.
  • The control uses a 20dp icon inside a 40dp state layer and a 48dp target size.
  • Selected icon and selected hover or focus state-layer treatments use md.sys.color.primary, while the enabled unselected icon stays on md.sys.color.on-surface-variant.
  • Hover, focus, and pressed state layers reuse the shared MD3 state-opacity ladder of 0.08 for hover and 0.1 for focus and pressed.
  • Disabled selected and unselected icons both use md.sys.color.on-surface at 0.38 opacity.
  • Adjacent text labels stay on the on surface color role regardless of whether the radio button is selected or being interacted with.

docs.title: Implementation Notes
docs.text:
• Model the radio button as a 20dp visual icon inside a larger 48dp hit target, with a 40dp state layer centered on the control.
  • Preserve the enabled unselected icon on md.sys.color.on-surface-variant; interaction states promote the unselected hover, focus, and pressed treatments to md.sys.color.on-surface.
  • Selected icon color stays on md.sys.color.primary across enabled, hover, focus, and pressed states; the pressed selected state layer is the only selected interaction state that switches to md.sys.color.on-surface.
  • The live viewer exposes no separate focus-indicator token family for radio button, so current MD3 spec coverage is limited to icon and state-layer treatments for focus.
  • The measurements figure did not expose additional reliably legible numeric values beyond the table entries above.

docs.title: Search MD3 Specs
docs.text: Source: https://m3.material.io/components/search/specs Collected: 2026-05-26

docs.title: Summary
docs.text:
• Search exposes two active token sets in the live viewer: Search - View for the activated search surface and Search - Bar for the unfocused bar.
  • The unfocused search bar keeps a 56dp container with 24dp outer margins, 4dp icon or label gaps, and a 30dp avatar; expressive focus reduces the outer margins to 12dp.
  • Activated search splits by layout: contained search keeps a rounded bar and results surface, while divided full-screen search uses a 72dp header with no rounding and 16dp internal icon or text spacing.
  • Primary surfaces stay on surface-container-high or surface-container-low, text and icon roles mostly stay on neutral or neutral-variant roles, and both search surfaces expose a surface-tint layer color of #6750A4.
  • Search bar and search view text both resolve to body-large typography metrics: Roboto 16pt/24pt 400 0.5pt.

docs.title: Variant attribution and implementation scope
docs.text:
Added when Search was implemented (SearchBar / DockedSearchBar). The viewer's Color group is not split by variant, so the tables below cannot say which of contained / Divided consumes those tokens. That was settled by hand; recording it here so it is not re-derived from a table that cannot answer it.

Only the contained (expressive) variant is implemented. Baseline / Divided is deprecated, so every Layout and Text / Divided (baseline) row is a non-target.

Token Attribution Basis search-view.container.elevation, search-bar.container.elevation Divided — not implemented surface-tint and elevation are the mechanism M3 superseded with the surface-container-* roles; the expressive samples show no shadow on either search surface search-*.container.surface-tint-layer.color Divided — not implemented same; the viewer flags the search-bar row with a warning glyph (noted in the table below) search-view.divider.color Divided — not implemented contained separates with contained.docked.bar-results.gap = 2dp, not with a line — which is what the two variant names contrast search-bar.contained.leading/trailing-margin (24dp) and search-view.contained.leading/trailing-margin (12dp) contained — implemented as one animated property the Measurements row Leading padding — Unfocused: 24dp, focused: 12dp is filed under Search bar; the two endpoints sit in different token sets only because the View set takes over after activation search-view.full-screen.*, search-view.contained.background.color contained, but out of widget scope the full-screen container is the application's screen to lay out; nuiitivet ships no full-screen search widget

Three containers, of which two are widgets:

Container Widget Search bar container SearchBar Docked container DockedSearchBar (bar + container) Full-screen container none — the app lays out its own screen and places a SearchBar in it

Also unimplemented, deliberately: search-bar.avatar.* and search-bar.contained.avatar.target-size (no avatar slot), search-bar.contained.trailing-actions.* (a single generic trailing icon instead), and any disabled state — the Search - Bar colour group specifies Enabled, Hovered, Pressed and Focused only.

Note one internal inconsistency in this document: full-screen.container.shape is listed under Common tokens in the table below, but the Implementation Notes at the end assign "no rounding for full-screen results" to Divided. Neither claim was relied on, since the full-screen container is out of scope.

docs.title: Implementation Notes
docs.text:
• Treat search as two surfaces in code: an unfocused search bar state driven by Search - Bar tokens and an activated search view state driven by Search - View tokens.
  • Expressive contained search should animate outer margins from 24dp to 12dp on focus, keep the bar at 56dp tall, and preserve the 2dp gap between the docked bar and results surface.
  • Baseline divided search uses 16dp internal icon or text spacing, a 72dp full-screen header, a 56dp docked header, no rounding for full-screen results, and extra-large rounding for docked results.
  • Body text for both supporting and input content resolves to body-large metrics, so the same typography primitive can back the bar and the activated header text.
  • The live viewer exposes the search-bar motion spring only through its source token name, so any motion implementation should treat the spring family as specified but derive the exact damping value from the broader motion token source if that repository surface needs it later.

docs.title: Summary
docs.text:
• Sliders expose six active token sets in the live viewer: one common Slider set plus five expressive size sets from Slider - Size - Xsmall through Slider - Size - Xlarge.
  • The common set fixes the baseline active and inactive track height at 16dp, the standard handle at 44dp tall and 4dp wide, and the enabled active color on md.ref.palette.primary40 (#6750A4).
  • Expressive size sets scale track geometry from 16dp to 96dp and add inset-icon tokens from medium upward: medium and large use 24dp icons, while xlarge uses 32dp icons.
  • Disabled states mute the slider onto neutral tokens with 0.38 active-track and handle opacity and 0.12 inactive-track opacity.
  • The measurements chart and token viewer disagree on a few geometry values, notably the medium handle height and the label container height; the discrepancy is documented below instead of being flattened away.

docs.title: Implementation Notes
docs.text:
• Treat sliders as a common behavior surface plus expressive size overlays: the Slider token set owns state colors, stop indicators, value indicator styling, and default track or handle behavior, while the size sets only patch the geometry.
  • The enabled common slider uses primary40 for the active track and handle, secondary90 for the inactive track, and full rounding on track, handle, and stop indicators.
  • Disabled styling is driven by neutral tokens and explicit opacity rows rather than separate disabled palette tokens for every surface, so the implementation should preserve both the base color and the opacity.
  • Medium-and-up expressive sliders introduce inset icons through size-set tokens, but the measurements chart remains the source of truth for final preset dimensions when it conflicts with the token viewer.
  • Because the measurements chart and token viewer disagree on the medium handle height and the label container height, geometry presets in this repository should prefer the charted measurement values and use the token viewer primarily for colors, states, and ancillary spacing.

docs.text: Source: https://m3.material.io/components/snackbar/specs Collected: 2026-05-26

docs.title: Summary
docs.text:
• Snackbar exposes one live component token set, Snackbars, and the visible spec context is Default, Light.
  • The enabled snackbar uses inverse roles: inverse-surface for the container, inverse-on-surface for supporting text and the optional icon, and inverse-primary for the action label.
  • Geometry is compact and fixed: the single-line container is 48dp tall, the two-line container token is 68dp, the container shape is extra-small rounding, and the container elevation resolves to 6dp.
  • The measurement figure shows 16dp leading content padding, 8dp trailing padding after the action, and a close affordance built from a 24dp icon with 12dp padding on both sides.

docs.title: Implementation Notes
docs.text:
• Treat snackbars as inverse surfaces rather than standard surface containers: container fill uses inverse-surface, action emphasis uses inverse-primary, and supporting or close-affordance content uses inverse-on-surface.
  • The component exposes two explicit height variants, 48dp for single-line and 68dp for two-line content, so layout code should switch variants instead of stretching a single base geometry.
  • Action typography maps cleanly to label-large, while supporting text maps to body-medium; that is enough to derive the preview-only *.type rows without custom typography tokens.
  • The optional close affordance fits a 48dp wide touch target when the figure's 12dp + 24dp + 12dp spacing is applied.

docs.title: Summary
docs.text:
• Tokens and specs expose five non-deprecated size token sets in order: Xsmall, Small, Medium, Large, Xlarge.
  • Each size set keeps between-space at 2dp and uses a fully rounded outer shape with size-specific inner corner behavior.
  • Inner corner sizes scale by size and increase for hovered/pressed states; selected trailing-button inner corner stays 50% across all sizes.
  • Measurements explicitly define unselected menu icon offset by size (XS/S -1dp, M -2dp, L -3dp, XL -6dp).
  • Measurements also state that split-button inner spacing should always be 2dp and that inner corner sizing varies by button size.

docs.title: Implementation Notes
docs.text:
• Drive split-button geometry from the size token set first (xsmall through xlarge), with a constant between-space of 2dp.
  • Keep leading/trailing horizontal spacing size-specific; those values increase significantly at Large and Xlarge and should not be derived from a simple linear scale.
  • Preserve state-specific inner corner transitions (hovered and pressed) and trailing-button selected inner corner (50%) for correct split-joint appearance.
  • Treat container.shape as preview-driven in this source; use concrete corner-size tokens where provided (inner-corner and Xsmall outer-corner) for implementation math.
  • Keep split-button color behavior aligned with standard button specs; selected state applies a state layer without changing the base color role.

docs.title: Summary
docs.text:
• Tabs exposes two active token sets in the live viewer: Tabs - Primary navigation and Tabs - Secondary navigation, both under the Default, Light context.
  • Both variants use equal-width tab sections, square containers on md.sys.shape.corner.none, 48dp label-only height, 64dp icon-plus-label height, a 1dp divider, and 24dp icons.
  • Primary tabs drive the active indicator, active label, and active icon from md.sys.color.primary, while inactive label and icon treatments stay on md.sys.color.on-surface-variant.
  • Secondary tabs keep the active indicator on md.sys.color.primary, but active label and icon treatments stay on md.sys.color.on-surface; inactive label and icon treatments remain on md.sys.color.on-surface-variant.
  • Both variants share md.sys.typescale.title-small for tab labels, use hover opacity 0.08, focus and pressed opacity 0.1, and expose a secondary-colored focus indicator with 3dp thickness and a -3dp inner offset.

docs.title: Implementation Notes
docs.text:
• Implement both tab variants as square-corner containers with equal-width slots, a 1dp internal divider, and 48dp or 64dp heights depending on whether the tab shows only text or both icon and label.
  • Reuse md.sys.typescale.title-small for tab labels in both variants; the extracted component rows resolve to 14pt size, 20pt line height, 500 weight, and 0.1pt tracking.
  • Keep the primary-tab active indicator, active icon, and active label on md.sys.color.primary, but keep inactive icon and label treatments on md.sys.color.on-surface-variant and inactive hover or focus overlays on md.sys.color.on-surface.
  • Keep the secondary-tab active indicator on md.sys.color.primary while leaving the active icon and active label on md.sys.color.on-surface; inactive label and icon treatments still use md.sys.color.on-surface-variant.
  • Model the focus affordance with md.comp.*.focus.indicator.*: both variants resolve to md.sys.color.secondary, 3dp thickness, and a -3dp inner offset, while hover uses 0.08 opacity and focus or pressed uses 0.1 opacity.

docs.title: Summary
docs.text:
• Material Design 3 text field specifications covering filled and outlined fields plus current select and autocomplete variants exposed in the live token viewer.
  • Five interactive states are represented across the current token sets: Enabled, Disabled, Hovered, Focused, and Error.
  • Values were resolved from the Material token table using the Light + Default + Expressive context when available, with Light + Default as fallback.

docs.title: Interactive (tappable) icons — design note
docs.text:
Investigated for #302 (2026-07-11).

The text-field token set models the leading / trailing icon as decorative only: the icon tokens are colors per field state ({hover,focus,error,disabled}.{leading,trailing}-icon.color) and a 24dp size, describing how the glyph is tinted while the field is in that state. Both hover.trailing-icon.color and the enabled trailing-icon.color resolve to #49454F, confirming the token describes field state, not a hover of the icon itself. There is no icon state-layer token in any text-field set — the only state-layer tokens are for the filled field's own container.

MD3 does not spell out a token for an interactive text-field icon. The governing principle is stated generally: "Apply states consistently across components," and the Enabled state description ("An enabled state communicates an interactive component… Enabled states use the default styling for each interactive component") means an interactive element is expected to carry the usual state layers. Following the Flutter and Jetpack Compose implementations, an interactive text-field icon is therefore realized as a standard icon button (md.comp.icon-button.standard.*), which brings hover (8%), focus (10%), and pressed state layers plus keyboard focusability.

Implementation: in TextField, a leading / trailing icon with a tap callback (on_tap_leading_icon / on_tap_trailing_icon) is built as a standard IconButton; a decorative icon (no callback) stays a plain, feedback-free Icon. Hit testing is handled by the framework's coordinate-translating widget tree (offset-safe; see #300), not a field-local rectangle test.

Known gap: the framework has no mouse-cursor-shape API, so the pointer does not change to a hand over the tappable icon (no existing widget changes the cursor either). Tracked separately in #316.

docs.title: Summary
docs.text:
• The primary token viewer exposes two non-deprecated token sets: Time picker - Dial and Time picker - Input.
  • Dial tokens define a 256dp clock dial with a 48dp selector handle, 8dp selector center, 2dp selector track, and 96dp x 80dp time-selector cells; the horizontal period selector expands to 216dp x 38dp.
  • Input tokens define dynamic outer container sizing with 96dp x 72dp time-input fields and a 52dp x 72dp period selector.
  • Both variants resolve their outer container elevation through md.sys.elevation.level3; the outer containers use 28dp extra-large rounding while selector and input subcontainers resolve to 8dp small-corner shapes.
  • Hover state-layer opacity is 0.08; focus and pressed state-layer opacity are 0.1 across the exposed interactive tokens.

docs.title: Implementation Notes
docs.text:
• Treat dial and input variants as separate widget implementations. The dial variant adds dedicated clock-dial geometry, selector center, selector track, and selector-handle tokens, while the input variant adds focused-container and focus-indicator tokens.
  • Shape and elevation rows are not fully exposed inline in the viewer. The detail popups resolve them through system tokens such as md.sys.shape.corner.extra-large, md.sys.shape.corner.small, md.sys.shape.corner.full, and md.sys.elevation.level3.
  • Typography .type rows are composite preview tokens. The viewer also exposes scalar font, size, line-height, weight, and tracking rows, which are the more direct implementation inputs.
  • The dial token set includes *.ignore clock-dial tokens marked with a warning badge. Keep them out of default implementation paths unless you intentionally need to mirror the source exactly.
  • The accessible Measurements tables for vertical and horizontal dial layouts currently expose the same numeric rows in the live DOM, so the page does not provide different orientation-specific numeric callouts beyond the shared table values.

docs.title: Toolbars MD3 Specs
docs.text: Source: https://m3.material.io/components/toolbars/specs Collected: 2026-05-26

docs.title: Summary
docs.text:
• The active toolbar viewer exposes five current token sets under the Default, Light context: Toolbar - Color - Standard, Toolbar - Color - Vibrant, Toolbar - Docked, Toolbar - Floating, and Toolbar - Floating - FAB.
  • The deprecated Bottom app bar (baseline) remains on the page in a separate viewer, but the spec explicitly marks it as not recommended and this document skips its token rows.
  • Docked toolbars are square 64dp containers with 16dp leading and trailing padding and 4dp to 32dp action spacing, while floating toolbars keep the same 64dp height with a full shape, 8dp internal side padding, 16dp horizontal edge margin, 24dp vertical edge margin, and 6dp elevation.
  • Standard color toolbars use md.sys.color.surface-container for the toolbar and unselected button container with selected buttons on md.sys.color.secondary-container; vibrant toolbars switch the base container to md.sys.color.primary-container and selected buttons back to md.sys.color.surface-container.
  • Floating toolbars with FAB add an 8dp gap between the toolbar and FAB, support 56dp and 80dp FAB sizes, use 24dp or 28dp FAB icons, and resolve their FAB corners and elevations from the MD3 large and large-increased shape tokens plus elevation levels 1 and 2.

docs.title: Implementation Notes
docs.text:
• Treat toolbar geometry and toolbar color as separate concerns: Toolbar - Docked, Toolbar - Floating, and Toolbar - Floating - FAB define layout and shape, while the standard and vibrant color sets define the actual container and action colors.
  • Prefer docked and floating toolbars for new work. The spec page keeps the baseline bottom app bar only as a legacy fallback and explicitly recommends the docked toolbar instead.
  • Floating toolbars share the same standard-vs-vibrant color split as docked toolbars, but floating adds a 6dp elevated container and distinct horizontal vs vertical edge margins.
  • The floating FAB variant needs two FAB sizes in addition to the toolbar itself: 56dp with a 24dp icon and 16dp corner radius for the expanded FAB, and 80dp with a 28dp icon and 20dp corner radius for the medium FAB.
  • The extracted values here reflect the live Default, Light viewer context. Dark, contrast, and platform-specific variants remain available through the underlying contextual token tree but are intentionally out of scope for this document.

docs.title: Tooltips MD3 Specs
docs.text: Source: https://m3.material.io/components/tooltips/specs Collected: 2026-05-26

docs.title: Summary
docs.text:
• The tooltip spec page exposes two current token sets under the live Default, Light context: Tooltip - Plain and Tooltip - Rich.
  • Plain tooltips are compact inverse-surface containers: 24dp high, 8dp padded, 4dp corner radius, with inverse-on-surface supporting text set in body-small typography.
  • Rich tooltips are elevated surface containers: 12dp corner radius, 3dp elevation, surface-container fill, on-surface-variant text, and primary-colored action text and state layers.
  • The current typography ramp resolves to Google Sans Text for plain supporting text, rich subheads, rich supporting text, and rich action labels.
  • Rich tooltip configurations allow an optional headline and up to two text buttons; the measurements figure only specifies padding, so overall height remains content-driven.

docs.title: Implementation Notes
docs.text:
• Plain tooltips can be modeled as fixed-height inverse surfaces with a single supporting-text slot. The extracted token set only exposes enabled-state styling, so hover or pressed container variants are not part of this component.
  • Rich tooltips split structure and action styling cleanly: the container owns surface, shape, elevation, subhead, and supporting-text tokens, while actions reuse primary-colored label and state-layer tokens with hover 0.08, focus 0.1, and pressed 0.1 opacities.
  • The current live spec resolves typography to Google Sans Text, not the older Roboto-based ramp that appears in some previously collected MD3 docs in this repository.
  • Rich tooltip height should be treated as content-driven. The spec only gives padding, elevation, and corner geometry, then documents five content configurations ranging from body-only to subhead plus supporting text plus two buttons.
